brief: Mortgage rates near three-year highs are weighing on housing demand. October existing home sales fell 5.5% MoM to 3.75 million, the lowest since August 2010, with weakness broad-based across most regions. Inventory rose to 5.1 months' supply from 4.4 a year ago, but prices still rose 0.4% YoY, so RJ expects housing activity to stay subdued. Following Tuesday's hotter-than-expected CPI, October PPI (due 8:30 AM ET) is consensus-forecast at +6.6% YoY headline, driven largely by fuel, and +5.0% core. A higher-than-expected core print would signal inflation spreading beyond energy, and together the two reports are expected to strengthen the case for a 25 bp Fed hike on December 9. Cleveland Fed's Hammack, who dissented for 25 bp last meeting, pushed back on Gov. Waller's earlier idea of a 50 bp hike, preferring smaller, less disruptive moves despite citing broadening inflation. RJ agrees, expecting 25 bp in December followed by an extended pause. Separately, NVIDIA's CEO resignation left the SOX down only 0.3%, with semis ex-NVDA up 2.3% and up 19% week to date. RJ stays positive on Tech on AI buildout visibility into 2027, with consensus calling for 67% industry EPS growth.
